channel.title: West Coast Plant Project — BC Native Plants, Seasonal Guides & Updates
channel.description: Pacific Northwest native plant research, Coast Salish ethnobotany, seasonal South Coastal BC planting guides, and Surrey Royal Heights Seed & Book Library updates.

item.title: What to Plant & Protect Right Now in November (South Coastal BC)
item.description: November in Surrey & Zone 8a is prime window for planting dormant native shrubs and oaks before winter freezes, direct-sowing cold-stratified meadow seeds (Camas, Nodding Onion, Lupine), and mulching garlic & overwintered brassicas.

item.title: December Coastal Gardening: Dormant Live-Staking, Cold Frames & Early Seed Orders
item.description: Keep cool-season kale and leeks ventilated in cold frames, take dormant hardwood cuttings of Red-Osier Dogwood and Pacific Ninebark, and reserve spring vegetable & native plant pre-orders.

item.title: Designing High-Pollinator Coastal Spring Guilds: Native Shrubs, Camas & Companion Beds
item.description: Combine early-blooming Red-Flowering Currant and Oregon Grape with Camas, Yarrow, Basil, and Marigolds to sustain bumblebees, mason bees, and Rufous Hummingbirds from March through autumn.

item.title: Host Plants & Insect Ecology: Why Native Canopy Species Anchor Backyard Food Webs
item.description: Insights from our 140,000+ host-plant insect dataset: how Garry Oak, Saskatoon Serviceberry, and Nootka Rose support dozens of native butterfly, moth, and pollinator species.

item.title: Summer Drought Resilience in Zone 8a: Deep-Rooted Natives & Living Mulches
item.description: Reduce summer watering in Metro Vancouver & Fraser Valley gardens using drought-adapted Garry Oak, Woolly Sunflower, Common Yarrow, and Coastal Wild Strawberry groundcovers.

item.title: Coast Salish Food Systems & Cultural Stewardship of Camas Meadows
item.description: Exploring Hul'qumi'num, Halq'emeylem, and SENCOTEN plant knowledge around Camassia, Gaultheria shallon, and traditional meadow stewardship across the Salish Sea.
